questions.text: क्रोमैटिन धागे (सूत्र) के न्यूक्लियोसोम में हिस्टोन कोर होती है एक :
questions.text_english: The histone core in a nucleosome of chromatin thread is a/an:
questions.solution: The core of a nucleosome is formed by eight histone molecules, which is known as a histone octamer. The negatively charged DNA wraps around this positively charged histone octamer to form the nucleosome structure.
questions.solution_hindi: न्यूक्लियोसोम का कोर आठ हिस्टोन अणुओं से बना होता है, जिसे हिस्टोन ऑक्टामर कहा जाता है। ऋणात्मक आवेशित डीएनए इस धनात्मक आवेशित हिस्टोन ऑक्टामर के चारों ओर लिपट कर न्यूक्लियोसोम संरचना बनाता है।

questions.text:
मादा जनन तंत्र में गर्भाशय के संदर्भ में कुछ कथन नीचे दिए गए हैं :
(i) गर्भस्थ शिशु के जन्म के समय गर्भाशय के पेशीस्तर (मायोमेट्रियम) में काफी तेज संकुचन होते हैं।
(ii) गर्भाशय एक संकीर्ण पथ, जिसे योनि कहते हैं, द्वारा गर्भाशय ग्रीवा में खुलता है।
(iii) गर्भाशय ग्रीवा तथा योनि की गुहा मिलकर जन्म नाल (मार्ग) बनाते हैं।
(iv) गर्भाशय की सबसे बाहरी पतली झिल्लीमय स्तर परिगर्भाशय (पेरिमैट्रियम) होती है।
(v) गर्भाशय श्रोणि भित्ति से टेंडन (स्नायु) द्वारा जुड़ा होता है।
दिए गए विकल्पों में से सभी सत्य कथनों वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Given below are few statements with reference to the uterus in the female reproductive system:
(i) The myometrium exhibits strong contractions during the delivery of the baby.
(ii) The uterus opens into the cervix through a narrow opening called vagina.
(iii) The cavity of the cervix and the vagina forms the birth canal.
(iv) The outermost layer of uterus is a thin membranous perimetrium.
(v) The uterus is supported by tendons attached to the pelvic wall.
Choose the option with all true statements from the given options:
questions.solution: Statements (i), (iii), and (iv) are true regarding the uterus. Statement (ii) is false because the uterus opens into the vagina through a narrow cervix, not the other way around. Statement (v) is false because the uterus is supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall, not tendons.
questions.solution_hindi: गर्भाशय के संबंध में कथन (i), (iii) और (iv) सत्य हैं। कथन (ii) गलत है क्योंकि गर्भाशय एक संकीर्ण ग्रीवा के माध्यम से योनि में खुलता है। कथन (v) गलत है क्योंकि गर्भाशय स्नायुओं (ligaments) द्वारा श्रोणि भित्ति से जुड़ा होता है, टेंडन (tendons) द्वारा नहीं।

questions.text: अनुलेखन प्रक्रिया की अवधि (समय) में, एक उन्नायक आरएनए से आबंधन के बाद, पॉलीमरेज उत्प्रेरित करता है तथा डीएनए के टेम्पलेट रज्जुक में क्षारकों को क्षार युग्मन के लिए उपलब्ध कराता है :
questions.text_english: During the process of transcription, after binding to a promoter, RNA polymerase catalyses and makes the bases in the template strand of DNA available for base pairing, with the bases of:
questions.solution: During transcription, RNA polymerase uses nucleoside triphosphates as substrates for polymerization. Because it synthesizes RNA, it specifically utilizes ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, UTP, GTP, CTP) which pair with the complementary bases of the DNA template strand.
questions.solution_hindi: अनुलेखन के दौरान, आरएनए पॉलीमरेज पोलीमराइजेशन के लिए न्यूक्लियोसाइड ट्राइफॉस्फेट को सब्सट्रेट के रूप में उपयोग करता है। चूंकि यह आरएनए को संश्लेषित करता है, यह विशेष रूप से राइबोन्यूक्लियोसाइड ट्राइफॉस्फेट (ATP, UTP, GTP, CTP) का उपयोग करता है जो डीएनए टेम्पलेट स्ट्रैंड के पूरक क्षारों के साथ युग्मित होते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एन्युप्लोइडी का उदाहरण नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not an example of aneuploidy ?
questions.solution: Aneuploidy is a chromosomal abnormality characterized by the gain or loss of a chromosome (e.g., Down's syndrome is Trisomy 21, Turner's is Monosomy X, Klinefelter's is XXY). Phenylketonuria is an inborn error of metabolism caused by a Mendelian single gene mutation (autosomal recessive), not by aneuploidy.
questions.solution_hindi: एन्यूप्लोइडी एक गुणसूत्रीय असामान्यता है जिसमें गुणसूत्रों की वृद्धि या हानि होती है (जैसे डाउन सिंड्रोम में ट्राइसॉमी 21, टर्नर में मोनोसोमी एक्स)। फ़ेनिलकीटोनूरिया एक मेंडेलियन जीन उत्परिवर्तन (ऑटोसोमल अप्रभावी) के कारण होने वाला चयापचय का जन्मजात त्रुटि है, एन्यूप्लोइडी नहीं।

questions.text: दुग्धस्रवण के आरंभिक दिनों में एक मानव मादा में माँ की स्तन ग्रंथियों से निकलने वाले प्रथम स्तन्य (खीस या कोलोस्ट्रम) में समृद्ध प्रतिरक्षी है :
questions.text_english: Colostrum secreted by the mother's mammary glands in a human female during the initial days of lactation is rich in antibody :
questions.solution: Colostrum, the yellowish fluid secreted by the mother's mammary glands during the initial days of lactation, is extremely rich in the IgA antibody. This provides essential passive immunity to protect the newborn infant against infections.
questions.solution_hindi: दुग्धस्रवण के प्रारंभिक दिनों में माँ की स्तन ग्रंथियों से स्रावित होने वाला पीला द्रव जिसे कोलोस्ट्रम (खीस) कहते हैं, IgA प्रतिरक्षी (एंटीबॉडी) से भरपूर होता है। यह नवजात शिशु को संक्रमण से बचाने के लिए आवश्यक निष्क्रिय प्रतिरक्षा प्रदान करता है।

questions.text:
दिए गए विकल्पों में से उन कथनों को चुनिए जो पुष्पीय पादपों में परागण तंत्र के लिए सत्य हैं।
(i) वेलिसनेरिया में, मादा पुष्प परागण जलमग्न परागकणों द्वारा होता है।
(ii) जोस्टेरा में, परागकण जल की सतह पर निर्मुक्त किए जाते हैं।
(iii) जल-परागित अधिकतर प्रजातियों में परागकण श्लेष्मक आवरण द्वारा आवृत होते हैं।
(iv) जल द्वारा परागण काफी दुर्लभ है तथा यह मात्र 30 वंशों तक ही सीमित है।
सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Select the statements that are true for pollination mechanism in flowering plants from the given options.
(i) In Vallisneria, the female flowers are pollinated by pollen grains inside the water.
(ii) In Zostera, pollen grains are released on the surface of water.
(iii) In most of the water-pollinated species, pollen grains are covered by a mucilaginous coating.
(iv) Pollination by water is quite rare and limited to about 30 genera.
Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution: Statements (iii) and (iv) are true. Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 mostly monocotyledonous genera. In water-pollinated species, pollen grains are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering. Statements (i) and (ii) are false; in Vallisneria, pollination occurs on the surface of the water, whereas in Zostera (seagrasses), it occurs beneath the surface of the water.
questions.solution_hindi: कथन (iii) और (iv) सत्य हैं। जल द्वारा परागण पुष्पीय पादपों में काफी दुर्लभ है और लगभग 30 अधिकतर एकबीजपत्री वंशों तक सीमित है। जल-परागित प्रजातियों में, परागकणों को गीला होने से बचाने के लिए एक श्लेष्मक आवरण होता है। कथन (i) और (ii) असत्य हैं; वैलिसनेरिया में परागण जल की सतह पर होता है, जबकि जोस्टेरा में यह पानी के नीचे होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा संयोजन ऑस्ट्रेलियाई शिशुधानी जंतुओं तथा अपरास्तनी के अभिसारी विकास का सही उदाहरण है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following combinations is a correct example of convergent evolution in Australian marsupials and Placental mammals?
questions.solution: Convergent evolution is seen when placental mammals and Australian marsupials occupying similar ecological niches develop similar adaptations. The Numbat (an Australian marsupial, also known as the marsupial anteater) shows convergent evolution with the Placental Anteater. Options A, B, and C pair organisms that do not represent correct convergent counterparts according to standard evolutionary charts.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिसारी विकास तब देखा जाता है जब समान पारिस्थितिक निकेतों पर कब्जा करने वाले अपरास्तनी (प्लैसेंटल स्तनधारी) और ऑस्ट्रेलियाई शिशुधानी जंतु (मार्सुपियल्स) समान अनुकूलन विकसित करते हैं। नम्बैट (एक ऑस्ट्रेलियाई शिशुधानी जंतु) अपरास्तनी चींटीखोर (एंटईटर) के साथ अभिसारी विकास को दर्शाता है।

questions.text: किसी कवक कोशिका से डीएनए को पृथक करने के लिए इसका उपयोग किया जा सकता है :
questions.text_english: Isolation of DNA from a fungal cell can be achieved by using :
questions.solution: Fungal cell walls are predominantly composed of chitin. Therefore, the enzyme Chitinase must be used to break down the cell wall and achieve the isolation of DNA from a fungal cell.
questions.solution_hindi: कवक कोशिका भित्ति मुख्य रूप से काइटिन से बनी होती है। इसलिए, कोशिका भित्ति को तोड़ने और कवक कोशिका से डीएनए को अलग करने के लिए काइटिनेज (Chitinase) एंजाइम का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए।

questions.text: मटर के एक लंबे पौधे का, मटर के एक बौने पौधे के साथ एकल संकर क्रॉस कराने पर प्राप्त संतति में लंबे तथा बौने पौधों का अनुपात समान था। जनक मटर के पौधों का जीनीप्ररूप (जीनोटाइप) ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: During a monohybrid cross involving a tall pea plant with a dwarf pea plant, the offspring populations were tall and dwarf in equal ratio. Find out the genotype of parent pea plants.
questions.solution: This is an example of a test cross. When a heterozygous dominant individual (Tt, tall) is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual (tt, dwarf), the resulting offspring will exhibit a 1:1 phenotypic ratio (50% tall, 50% dwarf).
questions.solution_hindi: यह एक परीक्षण संकरण (टेस्ट क्रॉस) का उदाहरण है। जब एक विषमयुग्मजी प्रभावी जीव (Tt, लंबा) का समयुग्मजी अप्रभावी जीव (tt, बौना) के साथ संकरण कराया जाता है, तो प्राप्त संतति 1:1 के फीनोटाइपिक अनुपात (50% लंबा, 50% बौना) को प्रदर्शित करती है।

questions.text: क्या होगा यदि एक जीन 50 ऐमीनो अम्ल वाले पॉलीपेप्टाइड की कोडिंग (कूटलेखन) करने वाले 25वें कोडॉन (UAU) से "UAA" में उत्परिवर्तित हो जाए ?
questions.text_english: What would happen if a gene encoding a polypeptide of 50 amino acids, 25th Codon (UAU) is mutated to "UAA"?

options_english.A: A polypeptide of 49 amino acids will be formed.
options_english.B: A polypeptide of 25 amino acids will be formed.
options_english.C: A polypeptide of 24 amino acids will be formed.
options_english.D: A polypeptide of 50 amino acids will be formed.

questions.solution: The codon UAA is a standard stop (nonsense) codon. If the 25th codon mutates to a stop codon, translation will prematurely terminate exactly at that point. Thus, only the first 24 codons will be translated into amino acids, forming a shortened polypeptide chain of 24 amino acids.
questions.solution_hindi: कोडॉन UAA एक मानक स्टॉप (नॉनसेंस) कोडॉन है। यदि 25वां कोडॉन एक स्टॉप कोडॉन में उत्परिवर्तित हो जाता है, तो अनुवाद (translation) समय से पहले उसी बिंदु पर समाप्त हो जाएगा। इस प्रकार, केवल पहले 24 कोडॉन ही अमीनो एसिड में अनुवादित होंगे, जिससे 24 अमीनो एसिड की एक छोटी पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखला बनेगी।

questions.text: मानव कल्याण के लिए ब्यूट्रिक अम्ल का बड़े पैमाने पर औद्योगिक उत्पादन में उपयोग किया जाने वाला सूक्ष्मजीव है :
questions.text_english: Large scale industrial production of Butyric acid for human welfare is done using the microbe:
questions.solution: Butyric acid is commercially and industrially produced by the microbial fermentation utilizing the anaerobic bacterium Clostridium butylicum.
questions.solution_hindi: ब्यूट्रिक एसिड का व्यावसायिक और औद्योगिक उत्पादन अवायवीय जीवाणु क्लॉस्ट्रिडियम ब्यूटिलिकम (Clostridium butylicum) का उपयोग करके किया जाता है।

questions.text: यह सिद्ध करने के लिए कि डीएनए आनुवंशिक पदार्थ है, अल्फ्रेड हर्षे तथा मार्था चेस द्वारा रेडियोऐक्टिव (विकिरण सक्रिय) जीवाणु (जीवाणुभोजी) का उपयोग करके अपकेंद्रीकरण चरण का सही ढंग से अभिचित्रण करने वाला विकल्प है :
questions.text_english: The correct depiction of the centrifugation step of the experiment conducted by Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase on using radioactive labelled phages to prove that DNA is the genetic material is:

options.A: कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता नहीं लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता लगा AND कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (32P) का पता लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिविटी का पता नहीं लगा
options.B: कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता लगा AND कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (32P) का पता नहीं लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिविटी का पता नहीं लगा
options.C: कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता नहीं लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिविटी का पता नहीं लगा AND कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (32P) का पता लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता लगा
options.D: कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिविटी का पता नहीं लगा AND कोशिकाओं में रेडियोऐक्टिव (32P) का पता नहीं लगा + अधिप्लवी में रेडियोऐक्टिव (35S) का पता लगा

options_english.A: No Radioactive (35S) detected in cells + Radioactive (35S) detected in supernatant AND Radioactive (32P) detected in cells + No Radioactivity detected in supernatant
options_english.B: Radioactive (35S) detected in cells + Radioactive (35S) detected in supernatant AND No Radioactive (32P) detected in cells + No Radioactivity detected in supernatant
options_english.C: No Radioactive (35S) detected in cells + No Radioactivity detected in supernatant AND Radioactive (32P) detected in cells + Radioactive (35S) detected in supernatant
options_english.D: Radioactive (35S) detected in cells + No Radioactivity detected in supernatant AND No Radioactive (32P) detected in cells + Radioactive (35S) detected in supernatant

questions.solution: In the Hershey-Chase experiment, radioactive sulfur (35S) was used to label the protein coat, and radioactive phosphorus (32P) was used to label the DNA of bacteriophages. After infection, blending, and centrifugation, the heavier bacterial cells settled at the bottom (pellet) while the lighter viral coats remained in the supernatant. Since only the viral DNA enters the bacterial cells, radioactivity was detected inside the cells for the 32P batch, with none in the supernatant. Conversely, the 35S protein coats remained outside the cells, meaning no radioactivity was found inside the cells, but it was heavily detected in the supernatant. Option A correctly represents these experimental results.

questions.solution: An antibody molecule, synthesized by B-lymphocytes, is characterized by a distinct Y-shaped structure. It is composed of exactly four interlocking polypeptide chains. Two of these are structurally identical long chains known as Heavy (H) chains, and the remaining two are identical short chains known as Light (L) chains. Because of this configuration, antibodies are often chemically represented as H2L2. These robust chains are held securely together by strong disulfide bonds, and the unique, highly variable regions located at the very tips of the 'Y' arms form the highly specific antigen-binding sites.
questions.solution_hindi: बी-लसीकाणुओं द्वारा निर्मित प्रतिरक्षी (एंटीबॉडी) अणु की एक विशिष्ट Y-आकार की संरचना होती है। यह चार पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखलाओं से बना होता है। इनमें से दो लंबी श्रृंखलाएं होती हैं जिन्हें भारी (Heavy - H) श्रृंखला कहा जाता है, और दो छोटी श्रृंखलाएं होती हैं जिन्हें हल्की (Light - L) श्रृंखला कहा जाता है। इसलिए, एक एंटीबॉडी को H2L2 के रूप में दर्शाया जाता है। ये श्रृंखलाएं डाइसल्फाइड बांड द्वारा एक साथ मजबूती से जुड़ी होती हैं और 'Y' भुजाओं के सिरों पर विशिष्ट प्रतिजन-बंधन स्थल (antigen-binding sites) होते हैं।

questions.text: जन जागरूकता तथा परामर्श के अतिरिक्त, एनएसीओ (NACO), विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन (WHO) तथा अन्य गैर-सरकारी संगठनों (NGOs) द्वारा समाज में एचआईवी (HIV) संक्रमण को फैलने से रोकने (रोकथाम) के लिए उठाए गए चार उपायों की सूची बनाइए।
questions.text_english: Other than public awareness and counselling, enlist four measures taken up by NACO, WHO and other NGOs to prevent the spread of HIV infection in the society.

key_points: Measure 1: Ensuring massive blood supplies in blood banks are rigorously tested and completely safe from HIV.
Measure 2: Strictly mandating the use of only disposable needles and syringes in public and private hospitals and clinics.
Measure 3: Advocating and ensuring the free distribution of condoms to promote safe sex practices.
Measure 4: Actively controlling drug abuse, especially the sharing of infected needles among intravenous drug users.

questions.solution:
Beyond simply raising public awareness, organizations like NACO and WHO actively implement several critical physical measures to halt the aggressive spread of HIV. Four key actions include: 
1. Vigorously ensuring that all blood stored in national blood banks is comprehensively tested and guaranteed safe from HIV contamination.
2. Strictly enforcing the exclusive use of disposable, single-use needles and syringes in all medical procedures within public and private healthcare facilities.
3. Extensively organizing the free distribution of condoms to encourage and heavily promote safe sex practices among the general population.
4. Actively launching targeted interventions to control severe drug abuse, specifically aiming to completely eliminate the hazardous sharing of infected needles among intravenous drug users.

जन जागरूकता के अतिरिक्त, NACO और WHO जैसे संगठनों द्वारा समाज में HIV संक्रमण को फैलने से रोकने के लिए उठाए गए चार प्रमुख उपाय हैं:

2. सार्वजनिक और निजी अस्पतालों और क्लीनिकों में केवल डिस्पोजेबल सुइयों और सीरिंज के उपयोग को अनिवार्य करना।
3. सुरक्षित यौन संबंधों को बढ़ावा देने के लिए कंडोम का मुफ्त वितरण सुनिश्चित करना।

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Which one of the three diagrams (i), (ii) or (iii) is the correct representation of the replicating fork of DNA replication? Explain your answer.

key_points: Diagram (i) is the correct representation.

Explanation: The primary synthesizing enzyme, DNA-dependent DNA polymerase, possesses a strict biological limitation: it can only catalyze polymerization in one specific direction, which is 5' -> 3'. Therefore, on the template strand running 3' -> 5', replication proceeds continuously (leading strand), while on the opposing template strand running 5' -> 3', replication is forced to occur discontinuously in fragments (lagging strand) pointing away from the fork.

sub_questions.solution: Diagram (i) is the only correct and biologically accurate representation of a DNA replication fork. This is fundamentally because the core enzyme responsible for replication, DNA-dependent DNA polymerase, carries a strict catalytic constraint: it can only synthesize new DNA strands in the 5' to 3' direction. Consequently, on the exposed template strand with 3' to 5' polarity, the new strand is synthesized continuously (the leading strand) advancing steadily towards the opening fork. Conversely, on the opposite template strand possessing 5' to 3' polarity, the synthesis must still occur 5' to 3', forcing it to occur discontinuously in short segments (Okazaki fragments) moving away from the fork.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Name the enzyme used in E. coli to join the newly synthesised fragments of DNA.

key_points: DNA Ligase.

sub_questions.solution: The specific enzyme utilized in E. coli to securely join the discontinuously synthesized Okazaki fragments of DNA on the lagging strand, forming a single continuous strand, is DNA Ligase.

questions.text_english: Explain what is meant by the term amniocentesis. How is this technique misused in India?

key_points: Explain amniocentesis: It is a specialized prenatal diagnostic technique wherein a small, targeted sample of amniotic fluid is carefully extracted from the uterus. Fetal cells in this fluid are cultured and analyzed exclusively to detect potentially fatal chromosomal abnormalities and severe genetic disorders.
Explain misuse: In India, this life-saving technique was heavily and illegally misused for prenatal sex determination, directly leading to an alarming societal increase in female foeticide.

questions.solution: Amniocentesis is a highly specialized prenatal diagnostic procedure wherein a doctor uses a fine needle to carefully extract a small amount of the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing fetus. The shed fetal cells within this fluid are subsequently cultured and karyotyped to conclusively detect the presence of severe chromosomal abnormalities (like Down's syndrome) or specific genetic disorders. Despite its immense medical utility, this technique is tragically misused in India for illegal prenatal sex determination. When parents unlawfully discover the unborn fetus is female, it frequently leads to the horrific practice of female foeticide.
questions.solution_hindi: उल्बवेधन (एम्नियोसेंटेसिस) एक जन्मपूर्व नैदानिक ​​तकनीक है जिसमें गर्भाशय से थोड़ा सा एम्नियोटिक द्रव (उल्ब द्रव) निकाला जाता है। इस द्रव में भ्रूण की कोशिकाएं होती हैं जिनका उपयोग भ्रूण में गुणसूत्रीय असामान्यताओं (जैसे डाउन सिंड्रोम) और आनुवंशिक विकारों का पता लगाने के लिए किया जाता है। भारत में इस तकनीक का भारी दुरुपयोग अजन्मे भ्रूण के लिंग का पता लगाने के लिए किया जाता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप कन्या भ्रूण हत्या (female foeticide) के मामलों में खतरनाक वृद्धि हुई है।

key_points: Name VDs: Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Genital herpes, Genital warts, HIV/AIDS (any two).

State complications: Pelvic Inflammatory Diseases (PID), severe complications leading to abortions, tragic stillbirths, potentially dangerous ectopic pregnancies, irreversible infertility, or even aggressive cancers of the reproductive tract (any two).

questions.solution: Two common Venereal Diseases (VDs), currently known as Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs), that frequently occur in human females are Gonorrhoea and Syphilis (or Genital herpes, HIV). If these perilous infections are completely ignored and remain untreated during their early stages, the pathogens can aggressively spread deeper into the reproductive system. This dangerous neglect can result in extremely severe complications, notably Pelvic Inflammatory Diseases (PID) and irreversible infertility (or dangerous ectopic pregnancies).

The basic scheme of the essential steps involved in the process of recombinant DNA technology is summarised below in the form of a flow diagram. Study the given flow diagram and answer the questions that follow:
(a) Name the specific enzyme that might have been used to make the multiple copies of foreign DNA before undergoing Step-1 of the process.
(b) How does the use of restriction enzyme EcoR I in Step-1 facilitate the action of DNA ligase to form the recombinant DNA molecule ? Explain.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Name the specific enzyme that might have been used to make the multiple copies of foreign DNA before undergoing Step-1 of the process.

key_points: Taq DNA polymerase (utilized in the Polymerase Chain Reaction or PCR).

sub_questions.solution: Before proceeding with cloning, if vast multiple copies of the target foreign DNA were required, the highly specific, heat-resistant enzyme Taq DNA polymerase would have been utilized during the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) process for massive amplification.

sub_questions.text: (ख) चरण-1 में प्रतिबंधन एंज़ाइम इकोआर I का उपयोग पुनर्योगज डीएनए अणु बनाने के लिए डीएनए लाइगेज के कार्य को कैसे सुविधाजनक बनाता है ? व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) How does the use of restriction enzyme EcoR I in Step-1 facilitate the action of DNA ligase to form the recombinant DNA molecule ? Explain.

key_points: EcoR I makes staggered cuts on both the plasmid and the foreign DNA, producing specific overhanging single-stranded stretches called 'sticky ends'.

Because both DNAs were cut by the exact same enzyme, their sticky ends are perfectly complementary. They readily form temporary hydrogen bonds with each other, bringing the DNA backbones physically close together, which immensely facilitates the enzyme DNA ligase in permanently sealing them to form recombinant DNA.

sub_questions.solution: When the specific restriction endonuclease EcoR I is utilized in Step-1, it deliberately makes staggered, off-center cuts within its palindromic recognition sequence on both the plasmid and the foreign DNA. This specialized cutting leaves prominent overhanging, single-stranded stretches universally known as 'sticky ends'. Because both pieces of DNA were cleaved by the identical enzyme, their sticky ends possess perfectly complementary base sequences. These exposed sticky ends eagerly seek out and form weak, temporary hydrogen bonds with each other, physically holding the foreign DNA and plasmid DNA together. This initial stickiness immensely facilitates the final critical action of the enzyme DNA ligase, allowing it to efficiently and permanently seal the sugar-phosphate backbones, thus successfully forging the recombinant DNA molecule.

sub_questions.solution: In recombinant DNA technology involving plasmids, the most universally favored and commonly used competent host organism is the bacterium Escherichia coli (E. coli).

questions.text_english: Explain how the interaction between a fig tree and its tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp is one of the best examples of mutualism.

key_points: Mutualism is an interaction where both species benefit and rely on each other entirely.

Benefit to Wasp: The female wasp uses the fig fruit (specifically the ovary of some flowers) as a completely safe biological space to lay her eggs (oviposition) and uses the developing seeds as a food source for her nourishing larvae.
Benefit to Fig Tree: While the wasp searches for suitable egg-laying sites inside the inflorescence, she inadvertently but reliably pollinates the fig flowers, ensuring the tree's reproduction.

questions.solution: The tight one-to-one interaction between a fig tree and its specific pollinator wasp is a classic, unparalleled example of obligate mutualism, wherein both interacting species gain massive evolutionary benefits and absolutely cannot complete their life cycles without the other. The rewarding mechanism operates flawlessly: the female wasp gains a highly secure, sheltered environment by depositing her eggs deeply within the ovarian locule of the fig inflorescence, and her developing larvae feed on some of the maturing fig seeds. Concurrently, the fig tree is massively rewarded because, during her frantic search for suitable egg-laying sites inside the syconium, the wasp actively and reliably transfers pollen, ensuring the essential cross-pollination of the fig flowers.

questions.solution: When visualizing this specific food chain, the resulting ecological pyramid of numbers is inverted (or spindle-shaped), directly contradicting the classic upright pyramid model. To correctly depict it, draw three tiered blocks. The bottom block (T1 - Primary Producer) is the narrowest, representing just 1 massive banyan tree. The middle block (T2 - Primary Consumers) is wider, containing the 20 insects that feed extensively on the tree. The top block (T3 - Secondary Consumers) is the widest, representing the 32 birds that heavily predate on the insects. This inverted shape occurs precisely because a single, gigantic producer possesses sufficient biomass to support numerous smaller primary consumers, which subsequently support an even larger population of small secondary consumers.

questions.text: किसी स्त्री (मानव मादा) में प्रसव प्रक्रम में शामिल तंत्रिअंतःस्रावी (न्यूरोइन्डोक्राइन) क्रियाविधि की व्याख्या कीजिए जिसके परिणामस्वरूप गर्भस्थ शिशु को गर्भाशय से जनन नाल द्वारा बाहर ढकेल दिया जाता है।
questions.text_english: Explain the neuroendocrine mechanism involved in the process of parturition in a human female leading to the expulsion of the baby out of the uterus through the birth canal.

key_points: Initiation: Parturition signals originate from the fully developed fetus and the mature placenta, which violently induce mild uterine contractions called the fetal ejection reflex.
Hormonal release: This neuro-reflex triggers the maternal posterior pituitary gland to release massive amounts of the hormone oxytocin.
Feedback loop: Oxytocin acts aggressively on the uterine myometrium, causing stronger muscle contractions. These stronger contractions stimulate further, continuous secretion of oxytocin.
Expulsion: This intense, stimulatory positive feedback loop continues, causing increasingly stronger and faster contractions that ultimately expel the baby out of the uterus through the birth canal.

questions.solution: Parturition, the process of giving birth, is controlled by a highly complex neuroendocrine mechanism. The critical initiating signals originate directly from the fully developed fetus and the mature placenta. These biological signals induce mild contractions in the uterine muscles, a phenomenon universally termed the fetal ejection reflex. This specific reflex sends neural signals that powerfully trigger the release of the hormone oxytocin from the maternal posterior pituitary gland. Once in the bloodstream, oxytocin aggressively acts upon the smooth muscles of the uterine myometrium, violently causing stronger contractions. A powerful stimulatory positive feedback loop is established: the uterine contractions physically stimulate the pituitary to secrete even more oxytocin, which in turn produces even stronger, relentless contractions. This escalating loop continues until the powerful muscular forces successfully and safely expel the baby completely out of the uterus through the birth canal.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रसव (बच्चे को जन्म देने की प्रक्रिया) एक अत्यंत जटिल तंत्रिअंतःस्रावी (neuroendocrine) क्रियाविधि द्वारा नियंत्रित होती है। इसके लिए संकेत पूरी तरह से विकसित गर्भ और अपरा (प्लासेंटा) से उत्पन्न होते हैं, जो हल्के गर्भाशय संकुचन को प्रेरित करते हैं, जिसे गर्भ उत्क्षेपण प्रतिवर्त (foetal ejection reflex) कहा जाता है। यह प्रतिवर्त मातृ पीयूष ग्रंथि (maternal pituitary gland) को ऑक्सीटोसिन हॉर्मोन जारी करने के लिए उत्तेजित करता है। ऑक्सीटोसिन गर्भाशय की पेशियों (मायोमेट्रियम) पर कार्य करता है और मजबूत संकुचन का कारण बनता है। यह संकुचन पीयूष ग्रंथि को और अधिक ऑक्सीटोसिन स्रावित करने के लिए प्रेरित करता है। गर्भाशय संकुचन और ऑक्सीटोसिन स्राव के बीच यह मजबूत धनात्मक फीडबैक लूप (positive feedback loop) लगातार मजबूत होता जाता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप अत्यधिक तीव्र संकुचन होते हैं और अंततः शिशु को जन्म नाल के माध्यम से गर्भाशय से बाहर धकेल दिया जाता है।

questions.text: चिकित्सीय परीक्षण (अन्वेषण) की अवधि में, पता चला कि शिशु में क्रोमोसोम संख्या 21 की एक अतिरिक्त प्रति है। उस विकार की पहचान कीजिए जिससे शिशु पीड़ित है। उसके भावी जीवन में उत्पन्न होने वाले संभावित लक्षणों का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: During a medical investigation, an infant was found to possess an extra copy of chromosome no. 21. Identify the disorder the child is suffering from. Describe the symptoms the child is likely to develop later in life.

key_points: Identify the disorder: Down's syndrome (Trisomy 21).
Symptom 1: The individual is characteristically short statured with a small, unusually round head.
Symptom 2: Features a furrowed, protruding tongue and a partially open mouth.
Symptom 3: The palm is characteristically broad with a distinct, singular characteristic palm crease.
Symptom 4: Physical, psychomotor, and mental development is severely retarded.

questions.solution: The presence of an extra, third copy of chromosome number 21 (resulting from non-disjunction during gametogenesis) causes a severe genetic condition known globally as Down's syndrome, technically classified as Trisomy 21. As the infant develops, several characteristic and debilitating symptoms will manifest. Physically, the individual will typically be noticeably short statured, possessing a small, abnormally round head. The facial features often include a furrowed, protruding tongue and a mouth that is habitually kept partially open. The hands are characteristically broad and stubby, invariably featuring a distinct, singular simian crease across the palm. Crucially, the child's overall physical, psychomotor, and mental development will be severely retarded, leading to lifelong cognitive impairment.
questions.solution_hindi: गुणसूत्र संख्या 21 की एक अतिरिक्त प्रति (ट्राइसॉमी 21) की उपस्थिति डाउन सिंड्रोम (Down's syndrome) नामक आनुवंशिक विकार का कारण बनती है। शिशु के भावी जीवन में विकसित होने वाले संभावित लक्षणों में शारीरिक और मानसिक मंदता शामिल है। व्यक्ति आम तौर पर छोटे कद का होता है और उसका सिर छोटा और गोल होता है। जीभ में खांचे (furrowed) होते हैं और मुंह आंशिक रूप से खुला रहता है। हथेलियां चौड़ी होती हैं जिनमें एक विशिष्ट हथेली की लकीर (palm crease) होती है। सबसे महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि बच्चे का शारीरिक, साइकोमोटर और मानसिक विकास गंभीर रूप से बाधित (retarded) रहता है।

sub_questions.solution: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is strictly defined as the total amount of dissolved oxygen that would be entirely consumed if all the organic matter present in exactly one liter of water were completely oxidized by aerobic bacteria. BOD serves as a highly accurate, indirect measure of organic pollution. When a water body receives a heavy influx of organic waste (like sewage), huge populations of heterotrophic microbes multiply rapidly to aggressively decompose this material. During this massive decomposition process, they consume vast quantities of dissolved oxygen from the water. Thus, a significantly higher BOD reading unequivocally proves that the water contains a dangerously high concentration of polluting organic matter.

questions.solution: Genetically Modified (GM) plants have been engineered to exhibit highly beneficial traits that revolutionize modern agriculture. Three major advantages include: Firstly, GM plants are engineered to be extraordinarily tolerant to harsh abiotic stresses, easily surviving extreme cold, severe droughts, high soil salinity, and intense heat, which normally devastate conventional crops. Secondly, by creating pest-resistant crops utilizing genes like the Bt toxin, farmers drastically reduce their heavy and environmentally damaging reliance on toxic chemical pesticides. Thirdly, genetic modification incredibly enhances the nutritional value of staple foods, a prime example being 'Golden Rice', which is specifically enriched with Vitamin A to combat severe malnutrition.

Study the diagram above and answer the following questions:

sub_questions.text_english: (a) How many alleles are involved in blood grouping?

key_points: There are exactly three distinct alleles involved in determining the ABO blood grouping system: $I^A$, $I^B$, and $i$.

sub_questions.solution: The ABO blood grouping system in human populations is governed by multiple allelism. Specifically, the gene 'I' has exactly three distinct alleles responsible for determining blood type: $I^A$, $I^B$, and $i$.

sub_questions.text: (ख) एक व्यक्ति का रुधिर वर्ग 'AB' है जिसके दोनों अलील प्रभावी हैं। इस प्रकार की आनुवंशिकता को किस नाम से जाना जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) A person having 'AB' blood group has both dominant alleles. What is this inheritance type called?

key_points: This highly specific type of inheritance is universally called Co-dominance.

sub_questions.solution: When an individual possesses the 'AB' blood group, their genotype is $I^AI^B$. Since both the $I^A$ and $I^B$ alleles are fully dominant and neither masks the other, they both express their specific sugar polymers simultaneously on the surface of the red blood cells. This unique phenomenon, where both dominant alleles are independently and fully expressed in the heterozygote, is officially called Co-dominance.

sub_questions.text: (ग) एक पुरुष का रुधिर वर्ग 'A' है, उसने 'B' रुधिर वर्ग वाली महिला से विवाह किया । क्या उनकी संतति 'O' रुधिर वर्ग वाली हो सकती है? एक क्रॉस की सहायता से समझाइए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) A man with 'A' blood group marries a woman with 'B' blood group. Can they have a child with 'O' blood group? Explain with the help of a cross.

key_points: State conclusion: Yes, it is biologically entirely possible for them to have a child with an 'O' blood group.
Explain condition: This happens only if both the father and the mother are strictly heterozygous for their blood types, meaning the man is $I^Ai$ and the woman is $I^Bi$.

Demonstrate cross: Mating $I^Ai$ with $I^Bi$ yields gametes ($I^A$, $i$) and ($I^B$, $i$). The possible fertilizations produce offspring with genotypes $I^AI^B$ (AB), $I^Ai$ (A), $I^Bi$ (B), and crucially $ii$ (O), perfectly explaining the 25% chance of an 'O' blood group child.

sub_questions.solution:
Yes, it is entirely possible for a couple with blood groups 'A' and 'B' to produce a child with an 'O' blood group. This specifically occurs if both parents possess a heterozygous genotype. If the man is heterozygous 'A' (genotype $I^Ai$) and the woman is heterozygous 'B' (genotype $I^Bi$), their gametes will carry either the dominant allele or the recessive 'i' allele. 
When we perform the genetic cross ($I^Ai$ x $I^Bi$):
The man produces sperm carrying $I^A$ or $i$.
The woman produces ova carrying $I^B$ or $i$.
The resulting fertilizations yield four possible genotypes in the offspring: $I^AI^B$ (Blood group AB), $I^Ai$ (Blood group A), $I^Bi$ (Blood group B), and $ii$ (Blood group O). questions.text_english: Explain how the loss of habitat and fragmentation drives plants and animals to extinction with the help of an example of habitat loss in the Tropical Rain Forest. Also write the effect of fragmentation of a habitat on the population decline.

key_points: Explain Habitat Loss: It physically removes the absolute primary space and crucial resources required for species survival, leaving them completely vulnerable to starvation and exposure.

Provide Example: The massive Amazon rainforest (the 'lungs of the planet') is being relentlessly cut down and cleared at an alarming rate explicitly for cultivating soya beans or for conversion into vast grasslands for raising beef cattle.

Explain Fragmentation Effect: When large, contiguous habitats are aggressively broken into smaller, isolated fragments by human activities (like roads or fields), mammals and birds that strictly require large continuous territories for hunting and mating are badly affected. This forces severe population declines and drives them toward extinction.

questions.solution:
Habitat loss is undeniably the primary driver relentlessly pushing countless plants and animals toward absolute extinction, as destroying a species' home removes its food, shelter, and breeding grounds. The most dramatic and tragic example of this is the ongoing destruction of the Amazon rainforest. Often referred to as the 'lungs of the planet' and harboring millions of species, massive tracts of this once-contiguous forest are being aggressively cut and cleared by humans exclusively for agricultural expansion, specifically for cultivating vast fields of soya beans or creating sprawling pastures for raising beef cattle. 
Furthermore, habitat fragmentation acts as a lethal secondary blow. When sprawling, intact habitats are carved up into small, scattered, isolated fragments due to human activities (like roads or settlements), it creates disastrous ecological consequences. Large mammals and specialized birds that strictly require vast, unbroken territories to successfully forage and mate find themselves trapped in insufficient areas. This severe geographical restriction leads to drastic population declines and forces these majestic species onto the brink of extinction.

sub_questions.text_english: (A) Define transgenic animals. Explain in detail any four areas where they can be used for human benefit.

key_points: Definition: Transgenic animals are organisms whose original DNA has been deliberately manipulated by humans to possess and permanently express an extra, foreign gene.
Area 1: Study of Normal Physiology and Development - They are explicitly designed to study how genes are strictly regulated and how they deeply affect normal bodily functions and complex development.

Area 2: Study of Disease - They serve as invaluable, living biological models for complex human diseases (like cancer, cystic fibrosis, and rheumatoid arthritis) facilitating deep investigation into disease progression and radically new therapeutic treatments.

Area 3: Biological Products - They are genetically modified to act as highly efficient living bioreactors, producing incredibly valuable human medical proteins directly into their milk or blood, such as alpha-1-antitrypsin utilized to treat severe emphysema.

Area 4: Vaccine Safety Testing - Highly sensitive transgenic mice are heavily utilized in pharmaceutical labs to thoroughly test the safety and efficacy of newly developed vaccines (like the polio vaccine) before they are ever administered to human populations.

sub_questions.solution:
Transgenic animals are biologically engineered organisms whose original genome has been deliberately manipulated by scientists using sophisticated recombinant DNA technology to permanently insert and actively express an extra, foreign gene (a transgene) from another species. 
These genetically modified animals are produced for several highly beneficial reasons serving humanity and science: 
1. Study of normal physiology and development: Scientists intricately engineer these animals to study exactly how specific genes are naturally regulated, how they interact, and how they profoundly affect the normal functions and complex developmental stages of the body.
2. Study of disease: Transgenic animals, especially mice, act as critical biological models for severe human diseases. They are engineered to carry the specific genes responsible for human ailments like cancer, cystic fibrosis, and Alzheimer's, allowing researchers to study disease progression in vivo and aggressively test novel drugs and therapies.
3. Biological products: Certain transgenic animals are transformed into massive biological factories. For example, transgenic cows (like Rosie) or sheep are designed to produce highly valuable and otherwise expensive human therapeutic proteins (like alpha-1-antitrypsin for emphysema) directly into their milk, making harvesting very efficient and cost-effective.
4. Vaccine safety testing: Before any new, potent vaccine is approved for widespread human use, it must undergo rigorous safety testing. Transgenic mice, genetically engineered to react biochemically similarly to humans, are heavily utilized to test the safety and efficacy of newly developed vaccines, such as the polio vaccine, ensuring absolute human safety.

key_points: Structure: It consists of a massive, sterile cylindrical vessel typically equipped with a curved base to facilitate the thorough mixing of reactor contents. Crucially, it possesses a sparger ring at the base.
Function of Sparger: Sterile air is violently pumped through the sparger, creating a massive storm of fine bubbles. This dramatically increases the surface area for maximum oxygen transfer.
Working: A central motorized agitator system continuously mixes the broth, ensuring oxygen and essential nutrients are evenly distributed throughout the massive culture.

sub_questions.solution:
The sparged stirred-tank bioreactor is a highly advanced piece of industrial biotechnology equipment explicitly designed for the massive, large-scale cultivation of microbes. Structurally, it consists of a giant, sterile cylindrical stainless-steel tank, usually featuring a curved base which actively facilitates the continuous, unobstructed mixing of the heavy liquid contents. Its defining structural feature is the 'sparger', a specialized ring located at the base of the tank. 
During its working operation, sterile compressed air is violently pumped directly into the sparger. The sparger acts like a showerhead, forcing the air out as a massive storm of extremely fine bubbles that rush up through the culture medium. This immense profusion of small bubbles dramatically and significantly increases the total surface area available for maximum oxygen transfer, which is absolutely critical for the aggressive aerobic growth of the microbes. A central, powerful motorized agitator (impeller) constantly stirs the heavy broth, ensuring that these oxygen bubbles and the vital nutrients are flawlessly and evenly distributed throughout every corner of the massive tank. Furthermore, the bioreactor operates flawlessly by relying on highly sophisticated, automated support systems. These include an intricate foam control system to manage bubbling, a precise temperature control system (using cooling jackets), a highly sensitive pH control system to maintain optimal acidity/alkalinity, and specialized sterile sampling ports that allow operators to safely withdraw small volumes of the active culture periodically to monitor process efficiency without compromising the sterile environment.

key_points: (i) Description: When resources like food and space in a habitat are absolutely unlimited, every individual has the complete ability to realize its full innate potential to reproduce, leading to massive, unrestrained geometric growth.
(ii) Equation: dN/dt = rN. Here, N stands for Population density at time t. 'r' stands for the intrinsic rate of natural increase (births - deaths), representing the biotic potential.
(iii) Name: Exponential growth curve (or Geometric growth curve).

sub_questions.solution:
When observing a population of any biological species residing in an ideal habitat where essential resources such as food and space are completely unlimited, the population growth follows a very specific trajectory. Because absolutely no environmental resistance exists to limit reproduction, every single individual has the complete ability to realize its maximum innate biological potential to multiply. This leads to a massive, unrestrained, geometric increase in population density over time. 
This phenomenon is mathematically encapsulated by the profound differential equation: dN/dt = rN. In this formula, 'N' represents the Population size or density at a given time 't'. The crucial parameter 'r' represents the intrinsic rate of natural increase. It is biologically derived by subtracting the death rate from the birth rate (r = b - d) and functions as an extremely important metric for assessing the sheer biological potential of the population to expand. 
This specific type of explosive population expansion is universally named the Exponential growth curve. When this mathematical relationship is plotted on a graph, carefully placing Population density (N) on the vertical y-axis and Time (t) on the horizontal x-axis, the resulting line does not level off; instead, it shoots upward exponentially, forming a classic, distinctly steep 'J' shaped curve.

During his pioneering and extensive explorations deep within the dense wilderness of South American jungles, the great German naturalist and geographer Alexander von Humboldt made a profound ecological discovery. He meticulously observed the distribution of flora and fauna and formally concluded that within any given region, species richness steadily and predictably increases as the area of explored territory increases. However, he noted a critical constraint: this massive increase does not continue indefinitely; it only occurs up to a certain threshold or limit, after which it plateaus significantly. 
This fundamental ecological observation is formally known as the Species-Area relationship. It is encapsulated mathematically by the equation: S = cA^z (where S is Species richness, A is Area, Z is the slope of the line, and C is the Y-intercept). When plotted on a logarithmic (log-log) scale, this non-linear relationship elegantly transforms into a straight, linear line expressed by the equation: log S = log C + Z log A. 
To graphically represent this relation for a wide variety of taxa, one must draw a graph placing 'Area' on the horizontal x-axis and 'Species Richness' on the vertical y-axis. The plot must clearly display a solid curve rising sharply and then leveling off (a rectangular hyperbola) labelled S = cA^z, and simultaneously display a straight, upward-sloping line originating from the same axis space representing the logarithmic scale, labelled log S = log C + Z log A.

(ii) How are multiple embryos formed in a citrus fruit? What is the mechanism known as ?

key_points: (i) Monocot Embryo Structure: It uniquely possesses only one single, massive, shield-shaped cotyledon, which in the grass family is specifically named the scutellum. The scutellum is situated towards one lateral side of the embryonal axis.

(i) Shoot and Root systems: At its lower end, the embryonal axis terminates in a radicle and root cap, which are securely enclosed in an undifferentiated protective sheath called the coleorhiza. The upper portion of the axis (epicotyl) contains the shoot apex and a few leaf primordia, tightly enclosed in a hollow foliar structure known as the coleoptile.

(ii) Mechanism in Citrus: In citrus fruits, multiple embryos are naturally formed because several diploid nucellar cells immediately surrounding the embryo sac start actively dividing, aggressively protrude directly into the embryo sac, and independently develop into numerous embryos.
(ii) Name of mechanism: This fascinating biological occurrence of possessing more than one embryo in a single seed is scientifically referred to as Polyembryony.

sub_questions.solution:
A typical monocotyledonous embryo, found commonly in plants of the grass family like maize or wheat, exhibits a highly specialized structural organization. Its defining feature is that it uniquely possesses only one single, massive cotyledon. This large, shield-shaped cotyledon is specifically named the scutellum, and it is situated laterally (towards one side) of the main central embryonal axis. The embryonal axis is distinctly differentiated into two vital ends. At its lower end, the axis terminates in a radicle (the future root) and a protective root cap, both of which are securely enclosed in a thick, undifferentiated cellular sheath called the coleorhiza. The upper portion of the axis, extending above the level of attachment of the scutellum, is the epicotyl. It contains the shoot apex (plumule) and a few delicate leaf primordia, which are tightly enclosed in a specialized hollow, conical foliar structure known as the coleoptile, ensuring safe upward growth through the soil.
In certain plants, particularly citrus fruits and mangoes, a single seed can astonishingly contain multiple embryos. This fascinating occurrence happens naturally because several of the maternal, diploid nucellar cells that physically surround the embryo sac become incredibly active. They start actively dividing, aggressively protrude directly into the protective space of the embryo sac, and completely independently develop into numerous functional embryos alongside the zygotic embryo. This biological mechanism, resulting in the presence of more than one embryo inside a single seed, is scientifically referred to as Polyembryony.

key_points: (i) Naming ducts: The male sex accessory ducts include the rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, and vas deferens.

(i) Structural organisation: The seminiferous tubules within the testis open into the vasa efferentia through the rete testis. The vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into the epididymis situated along the posterior surface. The epididymis then leads to the vas deferens, which ascends into the abdomen, loops over the urinary bladder, receives a duct from the seminal vesicle, and opens into the urethra as the ejaculatory duct.

(ii) Role of FSH: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) is secreted by the anterior pituitary. In males, it acts directly on the Sertoli cells located within the seminiferous tubules. It actively stimulates these Sertoli cells to heavily secrete certain specific protein factors that are absolutely essential for the complex process of spermiogenesis (the maturation of spermatids into functional spermatozoa).

sub_questions.solution:
The male sex accessory ducts in the human reproductive system are a highly organized network responsible for the safe transport and temporary storage of sperm. The core structures include the rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, and the vas deferens. Their structural organization follows a strict sequential pathway. The process begins deep within the testis, where sperm is produced in the seminiferous tubules. These closed tubules open into a network called the rete testis, which funnels the sperm into the vasa efferentia. The vasa efferentia physically exit the body of the testis and open into the epididymis, a highly coiled tube situated along the posterior surface of each testis where sperm mature and are stored. The epididymis seamlessly transitions into a thick, muscular tube called the vas deferens. This vas deferens sharply ascends out of the scrotum, enters the abdominal cavity, and loops tightly over the urinary bladder. Here, it merges with a duct coming from the seminal vesicle to officially form the ejaculatory duct, which ultimately passes through the prostate gland and opens into the urethra for expulsion.
The process of spermatogenesis is strictly regulated by hormones. Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH), a powerful gonadotropin secreted by the anterior pituitary gland, plays a paramount role in this regulation. FSH acts directly on the large, supportive Sertoli cells located precisely within the seminiferous tubules. Under the intense stimulation of FSH, these Sertoli cells actively secrete certain critical chemical factors and binding proteins. These specific factors provide crucial structural support and biochemical nourishment absolutely essential to drive the complex process of spermiogenesis, heavily assisting the physical transformation of immature, round spermatids into streamlined, highly motile, mature spermatozoa.
